QASHANI:12:93-98/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:93-98/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:93-98/r3.claim: Bringing the whole family means gathering all faculties into moderation: the heart mediates between higher and lower and restrains bodily pleasure-seeking.
QASHANI:12:93-98/r3.anchor: في مقام الاعتدال ومراعاة التوسط في الأفعال، فإن القلب متوسط

JISHUMI:v5p3715/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3715/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3715/r19.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for the grief they caused him, admitting they were sinners.
JISHUMI:v5p3715/r19.anchor: سل الله لنا المغفرة مما لحقك من جهتنا من الحزن إنا كنا خاطئين مذنبين

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: After seeing events unfold, the brothers recognize their folly, confess their sin to Jacob as they had to Joseph, and ask him to seek forgiveness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they had confessed their mistake before Joseph (sws), as referred to in verse 91

BURSEVI:v4p207/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p207/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p207/r1.claim: The brothers ask Jacob to seek God's forgiveness, admitting deliberate sins against him, Joseph, and Benjamin and appealing to his compassion.
BURSEVI:v4p207/r1.anchor: إنا كنا خاطئين متعمدين للخطيئة والإثم مذنبين بما فعلنا بك وبيوسف وبنيامين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r1.claim: The brothers invoke Jacob's fatherhood to stir affection and compassion; their admission of sin presents forgiveness and intercession as fitting for someone who confesses wrongdoing, and their confidence in his pardon explains why they simply ask him to seek forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r1.anchor: ونادوه بعنوان الابوة تحريكا للعطف والشفقة وعللوا ذلك بقولهم : ( ( انا كنا خاطئين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that by calling him father they appeal to his compassion: without his intercession they would be lost, but Alusi says this reading is unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : حيث نادوه بذلك أرادوا ومن حق شفقتك علينا أن تستغفر لنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p276#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p276#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p276#2/r4.anchor: {قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين} مذنبين

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:97/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:97/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:97/r1.claim: Someone who confesses a sin is entitled to be pardoned and to ask forgiveness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:97/r1.anchor: ومن حق المعترف بذنبه أن يصفح عنه ويسأله المفغرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r4.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for their sins; each pronoun plainly refers to its owner, so the text need not repeat the subject.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r4.anchor: ورد كل ضمير من هذه الضمائر إلى صاحبه في غاية الوضوح

BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r5.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r5.claim: Jacob's sons confess intentional wrongdoing against Joseph; the author cites a Prophetic report that when a servant confesses sin and repents, God accepts the repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r5.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن العبد إذا اعترف بذنبه ثم تاب تاب الله عليه )

DURR-FULL:v4p583/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p583/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v4p583/r9.claim: Jacob postponed seeking forgiveness for his sons until the predawn hours.
DURR-FULL:v4p583/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - في قوله (سأستغفر لكم ربي) قال: إن يعقوب عليه السلام أخر بنيه إلى السحر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2200/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2200/r1.speaker: يعقوب
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2200/r1.claim: A report says the brothers spent twenty years seeking forgiveness for their treatment of Joseph, but it was not accepted until Gabriel taught Jacob a supplication invoking God as the hope, aid, and helper of believers and beloved of penitents.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2200/r1.anchor: انا يعقوب ، واخوة يوسف اقاموا عشرين سنة يطلبون المغفرة مما فعل اخوة يوسف بيوسف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r5.claim: Jacob’s reply answers the good news; the uncoordinated قال follows dialogue style, and he addresses the other sons who entered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r5.anchor: جواب للبشارة لأنها تضمنت القول ، ولذلك جاء فعل { قال } مفصولا غير معطوف لأنه على طريقة المحاورات ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r6.claim: Jacob restates what he had said when his sons complained that he kept remembering Joseph.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r6.anchor: فخاطبهم بقوله : { ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون } فبين لهم مجمل كلامه الذي أجابهم به حين قالوا : { تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r7.claim: The sons’ request is repentance and admission of guilt, asking their father to seek God’s forgiveness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r7.anchor: وقولهم : استغفر لنا ذنوبنا } توبة واعتراف بالذنب ، فسألوا أباهم أن يطلب لهم المغفرة من الله .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p280/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p280/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p280/r8.claim: A report says the brothers sought Jacob’s prayer after Joseph had forgiven them because they realized that his pardon and Jacob’s pardon would not help unless God forgave them; they acknowledged their wrongdoing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p280/r8.anchor: روي أن يوسف عليه السلام لما غفر لإخوته، وتحققوا أيضا أن يعقوب يغفر لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p287#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p287#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p287#2/r1.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for what they did because he was a prophet whose prayers were answered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p287#2/r1.anchor: سألوه يستغفر لهم ما أتوا لأنه نبي مجاب الدعوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r9.claim: The brothers sought forgiveness because they had caused Jacob grief, which they could answer for only by honoring him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r9.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم أدخلوا عليه من آلام الحزن ما لا يسقط المأثم عنه إلا بإجلاله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r10.claim: They also sought the prayer of their prophet father, whose supplication would be answered.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r10.anchor: الثاني : أنه نبي تجاب دعوته ويعطى مسألته ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r11.speaker: الليث بن سعد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r11.claim: Al-Layth, transmitted by Ibn Wahb, says Jacob and the brothers sought repentance for twenty years; Gabriel taught Jacob a prayer, after which they were answered.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r11.anchor: فروى ابن وهب عن الليث بن سعد أن يعقوب وإخوة يوسف قاموا عشرين سنة يطلبون التوبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r12.claim: One answer is that Joseph’s words promised future pardon rather than reporting pardon already granted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r12.anchor: أحدها : لأن لفظ يوسف عن مستقبل صار وعدا , ولم يكن عن ماض فيكون خبرا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r13.claim: Another answer is that Joseph forgave them regarding his own right, while they still needed their father’s forgiveness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r13.anchor: الثاني : أن ما تقدم من يوسف كان مغفرة في حقه , ثم سألوا أباهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r14.claim: A third answer is that they trusted their prophet father’s response but did not know their brother was a prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r14.anchor: الثالث : أنهم علموا نبوة أبيهم فوثقوا بإجابته , ولم يعلموا نبوة أخيهم

MUQATIL:12:95-96/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:95-96/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:95-96/r5.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for their wrongdoing concerning Joseph.
MUQATIL:12:95-96/r5.anchor: استغفر لنا ذنوبنآ إنا كنا خاطئين } [آية: 97] في أمر يوسف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p204#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p204#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p204#5/r1.claim: The brothers ask Jacob to seek God's forgiveness for the wrong they committed against him and his son, admitting their sins and repenting.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p204#5/r1.anchor: سل الله مغفرة ما ارتكبنا في حقك وحق ابنك انا تبنا واعترفنا بخطايانا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r13.claim: The narrative omits their return from Egypt; this supports the view that Jacob’s earlier critics were relatives or grandchildren, since his sons were absent.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r13.anchor: في الكلام حذف، التقدير: فلما رجعوا من مصر قالوا يا أبانا وهذا يدل على أن الذي قال له

QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r14.claim: The brothers asked Jacob to seek forgiveness because they had inflicted grief that only his pardon could clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r14.anchor: وإنما سألوه المغفرة، لأنهم أدخلوا عليه من ألم الحزن ما لم يسقط المأثم عنه إلا بإحلاله

QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r15.claim: Anyone who wrongs another in person or property must seek release and disclose the wrong and its extent; the author rejects the view that a vague pardon is sufficient because details might change the victim’s willingness.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r15.anchor: وهذا الحكم ثابت فيمن آذى مسلما في نفسه أو ماله أو غير ذلك ظالما له

STUDYQURAN:12:97/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:97/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:12:97/r1.claim: This exchange happened after the brothers returned home from Egypt.
STUDYQURAN:12:97/r1.anchor: This conversation occurred after the brothers returned home from Egypt (Q)

STUDYQURAN:12:97/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:97/r2.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:12:97/r2.claim: Some say Jacob delayed seeking forgiveness, perhaps to see whether his sons were sincere and truthful.
STUDYQURAN:12:97/r2.anchor: Jacob delayed his prayer for forgiveness a certain period of time (Q, R), perhaps to ascertain whether they were being sincere and truthful

TAB-FULL:v13p367/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p367/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v13p367/r5.claim: A long report says the brothers feared their parents’ pardon was insufficient, asked them to seek God’s pardon, and received revelation twenty years later that God had forgiven them and covenanted future prophethood among them.
TAB-FULL:v13p367/r5.anchor: عن يزيد الرقاشي، عن أنس بن مالك، قال: " إن الله تبارك وتعالى بما جمع ليعقوب شمله، وأقر عينه، خلا ولده نجيا،

TABATABAI:12:96-99/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:96-99/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:96-99/r4.claim: The sons seek forgiveness for their deeds against Joseph and Benjamin; Joseph had already forgiven them.
TABATABAI:12:96-99/r4.anchor: وأما يوسف فقد كان استغفر لهم قبل

THALABI:v5p256/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p256/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p256/r4.claim: Jacob delays asking forgiveness for his sons until the night prayer; most commentators specify pre-dawn, when prayer is not veiled from God.
THALABI:v5p256/r4.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: أخره من الليل إلى السحر، وذلك أن الدعاء بالأسحار لا يحجب عن الله

THALABI:v5p256/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p256/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p256/r5.claim: At dawn Jacob asks forgiveness for grief and impatience over Joseph and for his sons' acts; God reveals that He has forgiven them all.
THALABI:v5p256/r5.anchor: فلما فرغ منها رفع يده إلى الله تعالى: اللهم اغفر لي حزني على يوسف

THALABI:v5p256/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p256/r6.speaker: محارب بن دثار
THALABI:v5p256/r6.claim: Muharib ibn Dithar says Abd Allah ibn Masud invoked forgiveness at dawn and explained Jacob postponed his sons' forgiveness until then.
THALABI:v5p256/r6.anchor: قال محارب بن دثار: كان عم لي يأتي المسجد، قال: فمررت بدار عبد الله بن مسعود

THALABI:v5p256/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p256/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v5p256/r7.claim: Ikrima from Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet explaining Jacob's promise to seek forgiveness as waiting until Friday.
THALABI:v5p256/r7.anchor: عكرمة عن ابن عباس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «سوف أستغفر لكم ربي، يقول: حتى يأتي يوم الجمعة

THALABI:v5p256/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p256/r8.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v5p256/r8.claim: Wahb says Jacob sought forgiveness for his sons every Friday night for more than twenty years.
THALABI:v5p256/r8.anchor: قال وهب: كان يستغفر لهم كل ليلة جمعة في نيف وعشرين سنة

THALABI:v5p256/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p256/r9.speaker: طاوس
THALABI:v5p256/r9.claim: Tawus says Jacob delayed until the pre-dawn of Friday, which coincided with Ashura.
THALABI:v5p256/r9.anchor: وقال طاوس: أخر إلى السحر من ليلة الجمعة فوافق ذلك ليلة عاشوراء

ELMALILI:12:96-98/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:96-98/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:96-98/r4.claim: The sons confess real guilt and remorse and ask Jacob to pray that their sins be forgiven.
ELMALILI:12:96-98/r4.anchor: biz hakikaten suçlu idik şimdi çok nâdim olduk.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:97/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:97/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:97/r1.claim: The sons confessed and asked Jacob to seek God's forgiveness, but because he remained hurt he delayed praying, perhaps until dawn or reconciliation, or to signal his grievance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:97/r1.anchor: Ya‘kūb’un, oğullarına karşı kalbi kırıktı, kendisinin affettiğine işaret etmekle birlikte Allah’ın affı için hemen dua etmedi

ZAJJAJ:v3p128#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p128#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p128#2/r1.claim: Khaṭiʾa/yakhṭaʾu and akhṭaʾa/yukhṭiʾu are distinct verb forms; an Imruʾ al-Qays line uses khaṭiʾna.
ZAJJAJ:v3p128#2/r1.anchor: قد خطئ يخطأ خطأ وخطأ، وأخطأ يخطئ إخطاء

QIRAAT-ER:12:97:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:97:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:97:9#1/r1.claim: The canonical ten-reading form elides hamza in khāṭiʾīna, preserving the same root and meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:12:97:9#1/r1.anchor: Hamza-elision variant (canonical 10-reading): removes ʾ from khāṭiʾīna → khāṭīna; phonological simplification

DAMGHANI:v1p157/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r7.claim: Khāṭiʾūn can mean sinners whose sin is not shirk.
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r7.anchor: خاطئون من غير شرك فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r5.claim: Khaṭaʾ can mean a sin that is not shirk.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r5.anchor: والثاني : الذنب ( الذي ليس بشرك ) . ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف :

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.claim: Joseph’s brothers did not ask him to forgive them or name their offense, using a light إن; to their father they explicitly requested forgiveness and admitted their sins emphatically with إنّا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.anchor: هم لم يسألوه المغفرة وإنما هو الذي دعا لهم بالمغفرة دون أن يسألوه حتى أنهم لم يذكروا الخطيئة التي ارتكبوها بحق يوسف
